text:
maya: noticing weird consolidation behavior after we added the new Mx-4 and Mx-8 GPU node types in eu-west. CA keeps leaving half-empty 8-GPU nodes and spins up 4-GPU nodes instead — cost is creeping up. anyone else seeing this?

juan: saw spikes yesterday, yup. looks like CA favours fewer nodes but our mix is confusing the expander. what expander are we running? :thinking: 

maya: --expander=least-waste currently (we switched last month). my suspicion: least-waste is calculating per-request but ignoring node-level taints/labels and per-NG min sizes, so it won't terminate older larger nodes even if pods could fit on smaller ones.

tess: can you paste the CA decision log when it chose to scale up instead of packing? logs often show the scoring.

maya: pasted below — note the score tie: it preferred launching a new 4-GPU NG rather than moving 3 pods into an existing 8-GPU node because of disruption cost.

```
I0306 09:12:34.123456 1 scale_up.go:412] Best option: add 1 nodes to ng-mx4 (score 0.45)
I0306 09:12:34.123789 1 scale_up.go:420] Considered ng-mx8 (available 5 GPUs) but disruption cost=0.8, fit score=0.44
```

sam: hmm. disruption cost being high means CA expects too many pods to be moved. are the pods using local-device plugins or GPU-allocated resources that prevent easy bin-packing?

maya: most are regular TF jobs using GPU, but several have nodeAffinity and tolerations for the Mx-8 NG (we experimented with dedicated pools). also some pods have hostNetwork:true for data-plane.

juan: OK. two levers: reduce disruption penalty (so CA will consider evicting and rescheduling), and make the expander prefer consolidation across NGs. for the former try lowering `--scale-down-utilization-threshold` or set `--scale-down-unneeded-time`/`--max-empty-bulk-delete` to more aggressive values. for the latter, try `--expander=most-pods` then tweak `--balance-sim` flags.

maya: proposed quick flags to test in staging (will run canary):
```
--expander=most-pods
--scale-down-unneeded-time=10m
--scale-down-unready-time=15m
--max-empty-bulk-delete=20
--skip-nodes-with-system-pods=false
--balance-sim=true
```

tess: also validate nodegroup min/max and pod disruption budgets. if NG-min for mx8 is >0, CA can't delete them. run this to list NG constraints:
```
kubectl get nodes -l nodepool=mx8 -o jsonpath='{range .items[*]}{.metadata.name} {.labels.nodepool-min}{"
"}{end}'
```

sam: another idea — add a lightweight daemon to annotate nodes with a consolidationHint label that CA (via a custom expander webhook we maintain) can use. i've prototyped a webhook that scores nodegroups by "waste-per-gpu" and forces balanced picks. could test that if flags alone don't help.

maya: I like the webhook approach as a backstop. for now i'll spin up the flag change in eu-west-staging tonight, run the jobset that replicates the fragmentation pattern, and report results in the morning.

infra-bot: deploy started: cluster/infra-config/eu-west-staging autoscaler-flags roll (user: maya) — 1742002000

juan: when you run the test, capture `kubectl describe pod` for a few of the moved pods and the CA decision log. also include cost delta (estimated) so we can justify changes to finance.

maya: will do. estimate: current fragmented week added ~2.4k USD to monthly GPU bill in eu-west based on raw hourly costs. if consolidation drops 30% we save ~720 USD/mo. noted. :thumbsup: 

tess: FYI, if we relax scale-down too much we risk churn during sustained bursts. maybe add an A/B: aggressive flags only on non-prod clusters for 48h then evaluate.

maya: agree — canary is non-prod. if it passes i'll propose a staged rollout with metrics: average GPU utilization, nodes-per-pool drop, pod evictions, and cost/hour.

sam: adding a tiny checklist:
- run jobset that simulates mixed 4/8 GPU pod sizes
- enable flags in staging
- capture CA logs + `kubectl get nodes --show-labels`
- run balance-sim compare (before/after)
- measure evictions 

maya: checklist noted, kicking off now. will post results in this thread.

infra-bot: deploy finished: autoscaler-flags applied (eu-west-staging) — 1742003200

maya: quick initial after 45m: more consolidation observed, CA terminated 3 mx8 nodes and replaced with 2 mx8+1 mx4 fewer than before, GPU utilization up ~18%. will run full metrics and cost calc tomorrow.

juan: great. if stable, let's draft an RFC for a controlled rollout and include the webhook as a fallback plan.

maya: will prepare RFC with before/after graphs tomorrow. thanks all.
